movement_source: row 'NIM (Excluding Notable Items, %)', column Full Year Sept 2024 -> column Full Year Sept 2025
headline: Westpac Group net interest margin (excluding Notable Items) decreased 1 basis point to 1.94% in FY25 (year ended Sep 2025) from 1.95% in FY24 (year ended Sep 2024). The margin comprised Core NIM of 1.81%, down 1bp, and a Treasury and Markets contribution of 13bps, which was stable. Net interest income rose 3% to $19,473m on average interest-earning assets up 3% to $1,002,856m, so the margin, not the balance sheet, was the drag. The results book's FY24→FY25 walk attributes the 1bp contraction to: Deposits -2bps (mix shift to lower-spread savings, term-deposit compression, lower rates), Loans -1bp (Australian spread competition and the auto finance sale outweighing NZ mortgage repricing) and Wholesale funding -1bp (higher funding costs as final TFF drawdowns matured), partly offset by Liquid assets +2bps and Capital & other +1bp (hedged capital earnings); T&M was a published zero bar. The investor discussion pack's composition table corroborates NIM 1.95%→1.94% and Core NIM 1.82%→1.81%.

drivers.columns: Full Year Sept 2025 vs Full Year Sept 2024
drivers.narrative: Largest drag. Deposit interest spread fell 2bps on a mix shift towards lower spread savings products, margin compression in term deposits and the impact from lower interest rates; earnings on hedged deposits were higher (partial offset).

drivers.columns: Full Year Sept 2025 vs Full Year Sept 2024
drivers.narrative: Loan interest spread 1bp narrower: higher spreads in New Zealand mortgages driven by fixed rate repricing were more than offset by tighter spreads in Australia due to competition and the sale of the auto finance portfolio.

drivers.columns: Full Year Sept 2025 vs Full Year Sept 2024
drivers.narrative: Wholesale funding costs 1bp decrease from the impact of higher funding costs, with the final Term Funding Facility (TFF) draw downs maturing in the prior year.

drivers.columns: Full Year Sept 2025 vs Full Year Sept 2024
drivers.narrative: Largest offset. Liquid assets contributed +2bps as average liquid assets rose by less than average lending assets (the bar includes other interest-earning assets).

drivers.columns: Full Year Sept 2025 vs Full Year Sept 2024
drivers.narrative: Capital and Other +1bp, primarily from higher earnings on hedged capital balances.

drivers.columns: Full Year Sept 2025 vs Full Year Sept 2024
drivers.narrative: Published zero bar: the Treasury and Markets contribution was stable at 13bps (0.13% in both FY24 and FY25), so it contributed nothing to the FY25 vs FY24 movement.

notable_items: NIM is reported excluding Notable Items; the only Notable Items in FY25 were hedging items (-$56m post tax vs -$123m in FY24) and do not enter the NIM walk.
limitations: Walk bars are printed in whole basis points; sub-components within each bar (e.g. hedged-deposit earnings inside Deposits) are described but not separately quantified for FY25 vs FY24.

The investor discussion pack's finer annotations (NZ mortgages +1bp, auto finance -1bp, consumer savings reprice +3bps, replicating portfolio +2bps, RBA rate changes -2bps, spread & mix -3bps) belong to its half-on-half 2H25 vs 1H25 walk, a different comparison, and were not used for FY attribution.
The FY walk does not split out a rate-timing (repricing lag) bar; rate effects sit inside the Deposits and Loans narratives.
NIM is published only excluding Notable Items; no statutory-basis NIM exists, so no cash-vs-statutory comparison is possible.
Liquid assets bar includes other interest-earning assets per the chart footnote.
